sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 6.4% a year from $38.5 billion in FY2016 to $67.6 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F201].
The path was cyclical rather than smooth: revenue rose 18.0% in FY2017 and 20.4% in FY2018, then fell 22.4% in FY2020 before recovering 22.1% in FY2021 [D42][D92][D198][D251].
The FY2017 rebound came from higher sales volume on improved end-user demand and favorable dealer-inventory changes [P86].
The FY2020 decline reflected lower end-user demand and dealer inventory reductions across all three primary segments [P59].
Operating income compounded at 28.6% against revenue's 6.4%, lifting operating margin from 3.0% to 16.5% [F202][F201][F21][F30].
In FY2025 Power & Energy contributed 5.2pp of the 4.3% revenue growth, with sales up 11.6% to $32.2 billion [D759][D463][D758][S102].
Construction Industries subtracted 0.6pp as sales fell 1.6% to $25.1 billion, and Resource Industries was flat [D766][D765][S105][D779].
The FY2025 top line rose on higher sales volume of $3.389 billion, partly offset by unfavorable price realization of $817 million [P13].
Profit grew slower than revenue: operating income fell 14.7% against revenue growth of 4.3%, an incremental margin of -69.1% [D464][D463][D488].
Diluted EPS fell 14.7% while net income fell 17.7%, as the diluted share count dropped 3.5% [D467][D465][D483].
FY2025 operating margin of 16.5% sits above the 14.3% window median but below the 20.2% FY2024 high [F30][D1123][F29][D1122].
The 3.7pp margin decline came mostly from cost of revenue, which added 4.2pp of drag as it rose to 66.2% of revenue [D476][D490][D441].

Operating profit fell $1.921 billion on unfavorable manufacturing costs of $2.148 billion and unfavorable price realization of $817 million, with manufacturing costs largely reflecting higher tariffs [P9].
Net margin fell 3.5pp to 13.1%, a smaller drop than operating margin's 3.7pp, as the effective tax rate rose to 24.0% [D477][F50][D476][D449].
Operating cash flow of $11.7 billion was 1.32x net income in FY2025, above the 1.13x conversion of FY2019 [F80][F40][D450][D132].
Free cash flow fell 11.2% to $8.9 billion, a 13.2% margin against the 11.9% window median [D469][F100][D447][D1129].
Capex rose 41.9% to $2.8 billion, 4.2% of revenue and 1.25x D&A, the highest capital intensity in the window [D470][F90][D446][D452].
Machinery, Power & Energy operating cash flow rose on lower working capital requirements and lower cash taxes paid [P4].
Net debt widened to $26.2 billion in FY2025 from $24.9 billion, as total debt grew 14.1% and cash rose 44.9% [D456][D403][D485][D484].
Net cash is -38.8% of revenue, below the -35.6% peer median and only the 43rd percentile of seven industrials peers [D457][D1152][D1151].
Buybacks of $5.2 billion plus dividends of $2.7 billion were 89.0% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count fell 3.5% [X140][X150][D459][D483].
Return on average equity of 43.5% ranks at the 100th percentile against a 23.3% peer median [D462][D1155][D1156].
Net cash has fallen for two straight years, from -$22.1 billion in FY2023 to -$26.2 billion in FY2025, as debt rose while cash stayed flat [D350][D456][D485].
Revenue fell 3.4% in FY2024, the only decline since FY2020, on lower equipment sales to end users [D410][P22].
Net income for FY2021 to FY2025 in the table is proxy-sourced and differs from the 10-K by up to 0.06%, so the 10-K figures should be used where precision matters [R3][X16][X20].
Segment revenue members sum to 219% of consolidated revenue in FY2025 because some are totals of others, so they cannot be added [R6].
Operating margin: a FY2026 reading below the 14.3% window median would confirm the FY2025 erosion; a recovery above the 20.2% FY2024 high would reverse it [D1123][D1122].
Capex: FY2026 capital expenditures above the FY2025 level of $2.8 billion would keep capital intensity at its window high of 4.2% of revenue [F90][D446].
Net cash: a further decline below the FY2025 -$26.2 billion would extend the two-year trend; a recovery back toward the FY2023 -$22.1 billion would reverse it [D456][D350].
